tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

1	# T1 foundation integration input for T4 and phase-1 review
2	
3	This file defines the concrete interfaces chosen under implementation-plan.md's Foundation protocol. Consume it together with root contract.md; it does not extend the language or authorize T4 before the phase-1 review/gates. Implementation and local checks are complete; individual independent review and the collective phase-1 READY TO ADVANCE verdict remain pending. No shared handoff/kanban edits, staging, commit, or deployment were performed by T1.
4	
5	## Shared imports available to parallel tasks
6	
7	- `from minisql.errors import MiniSQLError, LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, QueryRuntimeError, DataIOError`
8	- All accept `(message, line=None, column=None)`, including keyword arguments. `.message`, `.line`, `.column`, `.kind` are available; exception `.args` contains the message. Class-specific kinds are `Lex`, `Parse`, `Semantic`, `Runtime`, `IO`. DataIOError always has None positions, even if positions are supplied.
9	- SQL error strings are `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; data errors are `IOError: <message>`. No newline is added by the classes.
10	- `from minisql.model import Result`: frozen dataclass with `columns: list[str]`, `types: list[str]`, `rows: list[tuple]`, in that constructor order. Freezing prevents field reassignment, not mutation of the contract-required lists. It does not coerce or validate caller-provided values.
11	- Initial `minisql.__init__` reexports exactly those errors and Result. It does not import catalog, formatting, parser, or future engine/CLI modules. T4 owns final public integration.
12	
13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.
28	
29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.
34	
35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. 50

A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.

1	# T1 foundation integration input for T4 and phase-1 review
2	
3	This file defines the concrete interfaces chosen under implementation-plan.md's Foundation protocol. Consume it together with root contract.md; it does not extend the language or authorize T4 before the phase-1 review/gates. Implementation and local checks are complete; individual independent review and the collective phase-1 READY TO ADVANCE verdict remain pending. No shared handoff/kanban edits, staging, commit, or deployment were performed by T1.
4	
5	## Shared imports available to parallel tasks
6	
7	- `from minisql.errors import MiniSQLError, LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, QueryRuntimeError, DataIOError`
8	- All accept `(message, line=None, column=None)`, including keyword arguments. `.message`, `.line`, `.column`, `.kind` are available; exception `.args` contains the message. Class-specific kinds are `Lex`, `Parse`, `Semantic`, `Runtime`, `IO`. DataIOError always has None positions, even if positions are supplied.
9	- SQL error strings are `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; data errors are `IOError: <message>`. No newline is added by the classes.
10	- `from minisql.model import Result`: frozen dataclass with `columns: list[str]`, `types: list[str]`, `rows: list[tuple]`, in that constructor order. Freezing prevents field reassignment, not mutation of the contract-required lists. It does not coerce or validate caller-provided values.
11	- Initial `minisql.__init__` reexports exactly those errors and Result. It does not import catalog, formatting, parser, or future engine/CLI modules. T4 owns final public integration.
12	
13	## Lexer protocol
14	
15	`from minisql.lexer import Token, tokenize`; `tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]` lexes the whole string, including a terminal EOF token. `KEYWORDS` is the exact reserved set, a frozenset of uppercase strings; aggregate function names remain ordinary identifiers.
16	
17	`Token` is a frozen dataclass with fields, in order:
18	
19	| Field | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| kind | `INT`, `REAL`, `STRING`, `IDENT`, `QUOTED_IDENT`, `EOF`, an uppercase keyword, or the operator/punctuation itself |
22	| raw | Exact token source spelling, including any quotes |
23	| value | int/float for numbers; decoded str for names/strings; uppercase str for keywords; raw symbol for punctuation; None for EOF |
24	| start, end | Zero-based code-point offsets, end-exclusive |
25	| line, column | One-based token-start coordinates; only LF splits lines |
26	
27	In particular, a NULL token is a keyword token whose value is `"NULL"`; consumers derive the NULL literal's type/value from its kind, not from token.value. `007` decodes to int 7, `1e2` to float 100.0. Quoted names retain their case in decoded value; resolution later uses lower(), not casefold(). Unicode is accepted inside quotes, not in unquoted ASCII identifiers or numbers. Numeric continuation checking is ASCII as specified in feature-specification.md §5.2. Comments end only at LF. EOF has raw `""`, value None, start=end=len(sql), and the position immediately after all input, including trailing whitespace/comments.
28	
29	## Parser entry and ownership boundary
30	
31	`from minisql.parser import parse`; `parse(sql: str) -> minisql.ast.Query` fully tokenizes before constructing the parser, so LexError anywhere in the input precedes a possible ParseError. No catalog, name/function resolution, static typing, execution, or output formatting occurs here. For example, unknown function names, non-COUNT star calls, and multi-character literal ESCAPEs parse and await semantic validation.
32	
33	All AST records are frozen dataclasses, with inherited `start: int, end: int` fields first. Spans are code-point offsets into `Query.source`, end-exclusive. All sequence fields below are tuples. Optional tokens/nodes use None. All name/alias/operator/star/ESCAPE fields below are original lexer Token objects, not rewritten strings.
34	
35	### Expressions (`minisql.ast.Expr` subclasses)
36	
37	- `Literal(start, end, token)`: INT/REAL/STRING/NULL; token.kind preserves static literal kind and token.value preserves decoded numeric/string values.
38	- `Column(start, end, name, qualifier)`: name Token and optional qualifier Token. A qualified reference starts at its qualifier. Both IDENT and QUOTED_IDENT are accepted.
39	- `Unary(start, end, operator, operand)`: unary +/- or prefix NOT. The operator is its exact token.
40	- `Binary(start, end, left, operator, right)`: arithmetic, comparisons, AND, OR. Keyword operator kinds are uppercase, raw spelling remains unchanged; != and <> remain distinct.
41	- `IsNull(start, end, operand, operator, not_token, null_token)`: operator is IS, optional not_token is NOT.
42	- `Like(start, end, operand, operator, pattern, not_token, escape_keyword, escape)`: operator is LIKE even for NOT LIKE; escape_keyword is ESCAPE and escape is its STRING token. Runtime LIKE errors belong at operator; invalid ESCAPE length belongs at escape.
43	- `In(start, end, operand, operator, items, not_token, lparen, rparen)`: operator is IN even for NOT IN; items is a nonempty tuple of full expressions.
44	- `Call(start, end, name, argument, star, lparen, rparen)`: exactly one of argument Expr or star Token is present. Name is an ordinary or quoted name token. COUNT(*)'s star position is available directly.
45	- `Parenthesized(start, end, expression, lparen, rparen)`: explicit wrapper, including nested wrappers, with its own outer span. Parentheses are not erased during parsing.
46	
47	Precedence is unary signs > multiplicative > additive > one comparison/predicate > recursive NOT > left-associative AND > left-associative OR. Comparisons cannot chain without explicit parentheses; failure is at the second operator. Calls take one expression or star; IN has at least one expression. LIMIT/OFFSET take INT tokens, never signed, real, or parenthesized expressions.
48	
49	### Query and surrounding records
50	
51	- `Wildcard(start, end, star, qualifier)`: a Node, not an Expr; star Token and optional qualifier Token for bare * or q.*. Only projection items accept it.
52	- `SelectItem(start, end, expression, alias, as_token)`: expression is Expr or Wildcard; alias and as_token are optional name/AS tokens. Explicit AS and implicit aliases remain distinguishable. A SelectItem span includes its alias when present, while its expression span never includes that alias. Wildcards have no alias production.
53	- `TableRef(start, end, name, alias, as_token)`: name/alias Tokens; effective range name is alias if present, else name. TableRef span includes its alias.
54	- `Join(start, end, kind, table, condition, keyword, join_token, outer_token, on_token)`: kind is `INNER` for JOIN/INNER JOIN, `LEFT` for LEFT [OUTER] JOIN. keyword is the first JOIN/INNER/LEFT token; join_token is JOIN; outer_token exists only for LEFT OUTER JOIN; on_token is ON. condition is a complete Expr.
55	- `OrderItem(start, end, expression, direction)`: optional ASC/DESC Token; None means ASC. Span includes a direction if present; expression span does not.
56	- `Query(start, end, source, select_token, distinct, items, from_table, joins, where, group_by, having, order_by, limit, offset, semicolon)`: source is the entire original sql string. distinct is its DISTINCT Token or None. items is a nonempty SelectItem tuple. from_table is optional; joins are in source order. where/having are optional expressions. group_by and order_by are tuples, empty when absent. limit/offset are optional unsigned INT Tokens; use `.value` for the integer. semicolon is its optional token. Query span runs from SELECT through the last syntactic token, including a semicolon when present but excluding trailing comments/whitespace. EOF consumes all remaining input; only one semicolon is accepted.
57	
58	## Source metadata rules for T4
59	
60	1. Explicit output alias: `item.alias.value`, preserving query spelling without quotes.
61	2. Unparenthesized column: only a direct `isinstance(item.expression, ast.Column)` qualifies for its resolved CSV header. Parenthesized(Column) does not qualify.

1	"""Handwritten SQL lexer with code-point offsets and LF-only positions."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	import re
7	
8	from .errors import LexError
9	
10	
11	KEYWORDS = frozenset(
12	    "SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET "
13	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
14	)
15	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
16	_NUMBER = re.compile(
17	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
18	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
19	)
20	_NUMBER_CONTINUATION = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]")
21	
22	
23	@dataclass(frozen=True)
24	class Token:
25	    kind: str
26	    raw: str
27	    value: str | int | float | None
28	    start: int
29	    end: int
30	    line: int
31	    column: int
32	
33	
34	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
35	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
36	
37	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
38	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
39	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
40	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
41	    """
42	    tokens = []
43	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
44	
45	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
46	        nonlocal i, line, column
47	        text = sql[i:end]
48	        newlines = text.count("\n")
49	        if newlines:
50	            line += newlines
51	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
52	        else:
53	            column += end - i
54	        i = end
55	
56	    while i < len(sql):
57	        char = sql[i]
58	        if char in " \t\r\n":
59	            advance(i + 1)
60	            continue
61	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
62	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
63	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
64	            continue
65	
66	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
67	        if char in "\"'":
68	            quote = char
69	            end = i + 1
70	            decoded = []
71	            while end < len(sql):
72	                if sql[end] == quote:
73	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
74	                        decoded.append(quote)
75	                        end += 2
76	                        continue
77	                    end += 1
78	                    break
79	                decoded.append(sql[end])
80	                end += 1
81	            else:
82	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
83	                               else "quoted identifier")
84	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
85	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
86	            value = "".join(decoded)
87	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
88	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
89	        ):
90	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
91	            end = match.end()
92	            if end < len(sql) and _NUMBER_CONTINUATION.fullmatch(sql[end]):
93	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
94	            raw = match.group()
95	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
96	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else int(raw)
97	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
98	            end = match.end()
99	            raw = match.group()
100	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
101	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
102	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
103	            end = i + 2
104	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
105	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":
106	            end = i + 1
107	            kind = value = char
108	        else:
109	            raise LexError(f"unexpected character '{char}'", line, column)
110	        tokens.append(Token(kind, sql[start:end], value, start, end,
111	                            token_line, token_column))
112	        advance(end)
113	
114	    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", None, i, i, line, column))
115	    return tokens

1	"""Handwritten SQL lexer with code-point offsets and LF-only positions."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from dataclasses import dataclass
6	import re
7	
8	from .errors import LexError
9	
10	
11	KEYWORDS = frozenset(
12	    "SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET "
13	    "AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN".split()
14	)
15	_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
16	_NUMBER = re.compile(
17	    r"(?:[0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
18	    r"|[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+|[0-9]+"
19	)
20	_NUMBER_CONTINUATION = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.]")
21	
22	
23	@dataclass(frozen=True)
24	class Token:
25	    kind: str
26	    raw: str
27	    value: str | int | float | None
28	    start: int
29	    end: int
30	    line: int
31	    column: int
32	
33	
34	def tokenize(sql: str) -> list[Token]:
35	    """Tokenize the entire source, including a positioned terminal EOF token.
36	
37	    Kinds are INT, REAL, STRING, IDENT, QUOTED_IDENT, EOF, uppercase reserved
38	    keywords, or the operator/punctuation itself. Offsets are zero-based and
39	    end-exclusive; line/column are one-based. Values decode quotes/numbers;
40	    keyword values are uppercase and EOF's value is None.
41	    """
42	    tokens = []
43	    i, line, column = 0, 1, 1
44	
45	    def advance(end: int) -> None:
46	        nonlocal i, line, column
47	        text = sql[i:end]
48	        newlines = text.count("\n")
49	        if newlines:
50	            line += newlines
51	            column = len(text.rsplit("\n", 1)[1]) + 1
52	        else:
53	            column += end - i
54	        i = end
55	
56	    while i < len(sql):
57	        char = sql[i]
58	        if char in " \t\r\n":
59	            advance(i + 1)
60	            continue
61	        if sql.startswith("--", i):
62	            end = sql.find("\n", i)
63	            advance(len(sql) if end == -1 else end)
64	            continue
65	
66	        start, token_line, token_column = i, line, column
67	        if char in "\"'":
68	            quote = char
69	            end = i + 1
70	            decoded = []
71	            while end < len(sql):
72	                if sql[end] == quote:
73	                    if end + 1 < len(sql) and sql[end + 1] == quote:
74	                        decoded.append(quote)
75	                        end += 2
76	                        continue
77	                    end += 1
78	                    break
79	                decoded.append(sql[end])
80	                end += 1
81	            else:
82	                description = ("string literal" if quote == "'"
83	                               else "quoted identifier")
84	                raise LexError(f"unterminated {description}", line, column)
85	            kind = "STRING" if quote == "'" else "QUOTED_IDENT"
86	            value = "".join(decoded)
87	        elif "0" <= char <= "9" or (
88	            char == "." and i + 1 < len(sql) and "0" <= sql[i + 1] <= "9"
89	        ):
90	            match = _NUMBER.match(sql, i)
91	            end = match.end()
92	            if end < len(sql) and _NUMBER_CONTINUATION.fullmatch(sql[end]):
93	                raise LexError("invalid number literal", line, column)
94	            raw = match.group()
95	            kind = "REAL" if any(c in raw for c in ".eE") else "INT"
96	            value = float(raw) if kind == "REAL" else int(raw)
97	        elif match := _NAME.match(sql, i):
98	            end = match.end()
99	            raw = match.group()
100	            kind = raw.upper() if raw.upper() in KEYWORDS else "IDENT"
101	            value = raw if kind == "IDENT" else kind
102	        elif sql[i:i + 2] in ("<>", "!=", "<=", ">="):
103	            end = i + 2
104	            kind = value = sql[i:end]
105	        elif char in "+-*/%=<>(),.;":
106	            end = i + 1
107	            kind = value = char
108	        else:
109	            raise LexError(f"unexpected character '{char}'", line, column)
110	        tokens.append(Token(kind, sql[start:end], value, start, end,
111	                            token_line, token_column))
112	        advance(end)
113	
114	    tokens.append(Token("EOF", "", None, i, i, line, column))
115	    return tokens

17	        return node.token.value

20	                node.name.value)

1	# minisql: Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- Stack: Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- Package location: `minisql/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`), with `__init__.py` and `__main__.py`.
7	- Entry points: `python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]` from repo root; `import minisql; minisql.connect(DIR).execute(SQL)`.
8	- Do not use `sqlite3` or any existing SQL engine or parser.
9	
10	## Functional requirements
11	
12	- **R1** Importable as `minisql`, runnable as `python -m minisql`; standard-library imports only, never `sqlite3` or any SQL engine/parser.
13	- **R2** Tables load from the data directory per the data contract.
14	- **R3** Column types are inferred per the inference rules; empty fields are NULL.
15	- **R4** The tokenizer implements the lexical rules.
16	- **R5** The parser implements the grammar and precedence table.
17	- **R6** Keywords and all names resolve case-insensitively.
18	- **R7** Expressions are statically typed; violations are SemanticErrors raised before any row is evaluated.
19	- **R8** Arithmetic follows the numeric rules, including division by zero.
20	- **R9** Predicates follow three-valued logic.
21	- **R10** Projection supports `*`, `t.*`, expressions, aliases and the output naming rule.
22	- **R11** INNER and LEFT joins follow nested-loop semantics and order.
23	- **R12** Grouping, `HAVING` and aggregates follow the aggregate rules, including empty input.
24	- **R13** `DISTINCT` keeps first occurrences.
25	- **R14** `ORDER BY` supports aliases, ordinals, expressions, multiple keys, `ASC`/`DESC`; NULLs smallest; stable ties.
26	- **R15** `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` take non-negative integer literals.
27	- **R16** Clauses evaluate in the defined order; `AND`/`OR` short-circuit.
28	- **R17** The library API matches the contract.
29	- **R18** CSV and table formats match byte-for-byte.
30	- **R19** The one-shot CLI follows the output and exit-code rules.
31	- **R20** The REPL follows the prompt, buffering, command and exit rules.
32	- **R21** Errors use the specified classes, format, templates and positions.
33	
34	## Language reference
35	
36	### Lexical rules
37	
38	- Whitespace: space, tab, `\r`, `\n`. Comments: `--` to end of line.
39	- Lines split on `\n` only; line and column are 1-based; column counts code points; tab and `\r` count as one column.
40	- Keywords (reserved, case-insensitive): `SELECT DISTINCT FROM WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER ASC DESC LIMIT OFFSET AS JOIN INNER LEFT OUTER ON AND OR NOT IS NULL LIKE ESCAPE IN`.
41	- Unquoted identifier: `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, not a keyword. Quoted identifier: `"..."` with `""` for a literal `"`; may contain any character and may equal a keyword. Function names (`COUNT SUM AVG MIN MAX`) are ordinary identifiers.
42	- String literal: `'...'` with `''` for a literal `'`; may span lines; no backslash escapes (`\` is literal).
43	- INTEGER literal: `[0-9]+`. REAL literal: `[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, `\.[0-9]+([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`, or `[0-9]+[eE][+-]?[0-9]+`. A numeric literal immediately followed by a letter, digit, `_` or `.` is a LexError (`invalid number literal`). Signs are unary operators.
44	- Operators: `+ - * / % = <> != < <= > >= ( ) , . * ;`.
45	
46	### Grammar (EBNF)
47	
48	```
49	query     = "SELECT" ["DISTINCT"] item {"," item}
50	            ["FROM" tableref {join}] ["WHERE" expr]
51	            ["GROUP" "BY" expr {"," expr}] ["HAVING" expr]
52	            ["ORDER" "BY" order {"," order}]
53	            ["LIMIT" INT] ["OFFSET" INT] [";"] EOF ;
54	item      = "*" | name "." "*" | expr [["AS"] name] ;
55	tableref  = name [["AS"] name] ;
56	join      = (["INNER"] "JOIN" | "LEFT" ["OUTER"] "JOIN") tableref "ON" expr ;
57	order     = expr ["ASC" | "DESC"] ;
58	expr      = and {"OR" and} ;
59	and       = not {"AND" not} ;
60	not       = "NOT" not | cmp ;
61	cmp       = add [ cmpop add | "IS" ["NOT"] "NULL"
62	                | ["NOT"] "LIKE" add ["ESCAPE" STRING]
63	                | ["NOT"] "IN" "(" expr {"," expr} ")" ] ;
64	cmpop     = "=" | "<>" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ;
65	add       = mul {("+" | "-") mul} ;
66	mul       = unary {("*" | "/" | "%") unary} ;
67	unary     = ("-" | "+") unary | primary ;
68	primary   = INT | REAL | STRING | "NULL" | call | colref | "(" expr ")" ;
69	call      = name "(" ("*" | expr) ")" ;
70	colref    = name ["." name] ;
71	name      = IDENT | QUOTED_IDENT ;
72	```
73	
74	`FROM` is optional; without it the query runs over exactly one empty row. A table alias makes the table name unusable as a qualifier in that query.
75	
76	### Precedence (highest first)
77	
78	| Level | Operators | Associativity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| 1 | unary `-`, `+` | right |
81	| 2 | `*` `/` `%` | left |
82	| 3 | binary `+` `-` | left |
83	| 4 | `= <> != < <= > >=`, `IS [NOT] NULL`, `[NOT] LIKE`, `[NOT] IN` | none (`a = b = c` is a ParseError at the second operator) |
84	| 5 | `NOT` | right |
85	| 6 | `AND` | left |
86	| 7 | `OR` | left |
87	
88	### Types and values
89	
90	- Static types: `INTEGER` (`int`), `REAL` (`float`), `TEXT` (`str`), `NULL` (bare `NULL` literal only). Any value may be `None`; never `bool`. Comparison, logical, `IS`, `LIKE`, `IN` yield INTEGER `1`, `0` or NULL.
91	- Arithmetic operands must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type. Result type: REAL if either operand is REAL; else NULL if both are NULL; else INTEGER. Unary minus/plus keeps its operand type.
92	- Comparisons (`=`, `<>`, `IN` items, `MIN`/`MAX`, ordering) require both sides numeric (INTEGER/REAL mixed freely, compared numerically) or both TEXT, or either side NULL type. TEXT compares by Python `str` ordering (code points, case-sensitive).
93	- `LIKE` operands and `ESCAPE` must be TEXT or NULL. `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` operands and `WHERE`/`ON`/`HAVING` conditions must be INTEGER, REAL or NULL type; nonzero is true, zero is false, NULL is unknown.
94	- Integer `/` truncates toward zero (`-7 / 2` = `-3`); integer `%` takes the sign of the dividend (`-7 % 2` = `-1`, `7 % -2` = `1`). REAL `/` is float division; REAL `%` is `math.fmod`.
95	- If either arithmetic operand is NULL the result is NULL (checked first). Otherwise a zero divisor for `/` or `%` (INTEGER or REAL) raises RuntimeError `division by zero` at the operator.
96	
97	### NULL and predicates
98	
99	- Any comparison with a NULL operand is NULL. `NOT NULL` is NULL. `AND`: false if either side false, else NULL if either NULL, else true. `OR`: true if either true, else NULL if either NULL, else false.
100	- `x IS NULL` / `x IS NOT NULL` return 1/0, never NULL.
101	- `x [NOT] IN (list)`: NULL if `x` is NULL; 1 if some item equals `x`; else NULL if any item is NULL; else 0. `NOT IN` negates with 3VL.
102	- `LIKE`: whole-string, case-sensitive; `%` matches any sequence (including empty), `_` exactly one character. With `ESCAPE 'c'`, `c` followed by `%`, `_` or `c` matches that character literally; `c` followed by anything else or at pattern end raises RuntimeError `invalid LIKE pattern` at the `LIKE` token. `ESCAPE` must be a one-character string literal. Any NULL operand gives NULL.
103	- Equality for `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` treats NULL as equal to NULL; join conditions follow normal 3VL, so NULL never matches.
104	
105	### Type inference
106	
107	For each column, over its non-empty raw fields (no trimming): if every field fully matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` the column is INTEGER (`int(field)`); else if every field fully matches `[+-]?([0-9]+\.[0-9]*|\.[0-9]+|[0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?` it is REAL (`float(field)`); else TEXT (fields kept verbatim, including numeric-looking ones). A column with no non-empty fields is TEXT. Empty fields (quoted or not) are NULL in every type. Consequently `" 1"` makes a column TEXT, `007` is INTEGER `7`, and `1`, `2.5` makes a REAL column.
108	
109	## Interface contract
110	
111	### Data directory
112	
113	- `--data DIR` (default `.`); library `connect(DIR)`. A missing or non-directory `DIR` is an IOError: `connect(DIR)` raises `DataIOError` immediately, and the one-shot CLI reports it and exits 3 before lexing the SQL.
114	- A table is any regular file directly in `DIR` whose name ends in `.csv` (case-insensitive). Table name = file stem; lookup is case-insensitive. Two files whose stems are equal case-insensitively make every reference to that name an IOError `ambiguous table file '<name>'`.
115	- Files are read on each `execute` with `encoding='utf-8-sig'`, `newline=''` and `csv.reader(f, strict=True)` (default dialect). Only the tables referenced in `FROM`/`JOIN` are read; any other file in `DIR`, however malformed, never affects a query. `tables()` lists stems without reading file contents.
116	- Row 1 is the header; names are used verbatim. Empty header name, or duplicate names (case-insensitive), is an IOError. Lines yielding zero fields are skipped. A record with a different field count than the header is IOError `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, where N is the reader's `line_num` after that record.
117	
118	### Name resolution and output names
119	
120	- Column reference `c` searches all tables in `FROM`; `q.c` searches the table whose range name (alias, else table name) is `q`. Zero matches: unknown column; more than one: ambiguous column. Duplicate range names are a SemanticError. An `ON` condition sees only tables introduced before or in its own join; later tables are unknown there. Joins associate left.
121	- `*` expands to all columns of all tables in `FROM` order; `t.*` to that table's columns. Duplicate output names are allowed.
122	- Output name: the alias as written (quotes removed); else for an unparenthesized column reference, the column's header name as in the CSV; else the verbatim source text of the item from its first to last character (e.g. `COUNT(*)`, `a + 1`, `(a)`).
123	
124	### Aggregates and grouping
125	
126	- A query is an aggregate query if it has `GROUP BY`, `HAVING`, or an aggregate call in the select list or `ORDER BY`.
127	- `COUNT(*)` counts rows; `COUNT(e)` counts non-NULL values (INTEGER). `SUM` of INTEGER is INTEGER, of REAL is REAL. `AVG` is REAL. `MIN`/`MAX` keep the argument type. All ignore NULLs. Over zero non-NULL values `COUNT` is `0`, others NULL. `SUM`/`AVG` need numeric arguments; only `COUNT` accepts `*`.
128	- Without `GROUP BY` the whole filtered input (after `WHERE`) forms a single group, even when empty; without `HAVING` the query yields exactly one row, and `HAVING` filters that group, yielding 0 or 1 row (1 row over empty input when `HAVING` is true, e.g. `HAVING COUNT(*) = 0`). With `GROUP BY`, empty input yields zero rows; groups appear in first-seen order unless ordered.
129	- In an aggregate query, every select, `HAVING` and `ORDER BY` expression must be built from aggregate calls, literals, and subexpressions structurally identical to a `GROUP BY` expression (same resolved columns, operators and literals). `*` is not allowed. Aggregates are not allowed in `WHERE`, `ON`, `GROUP BY`, or inside another aggregate.
130	
131	### ORDER BY, DISTINCT, LIMIT
132	
133	- An `ORDER BY` item that is a bare INTEGER literal is a 1-based output ordinal, counted after `*` expansion. A bare identifier equal to exactly one select-item alias (written with or without `AS`) refers to that output column (two such aliases: ambiguous column). Otherwise it is an expression over input rows (or groups).
134	- With `DISTINCT`, each `ORDER BY` item must be an ordinal, an alias, or structurally identical to a select expression.
135	- Sorting is stable; ties keep pre-sort order for both `ASC` and `DESC`. NULL sorts before every value (first in `ASC`, last in `DESC`).
136	- `LIMIT 0` yields no rows; `OFFSET` past the end yields no rows.
137	
138	### Evaluation order
139	
140	1. `FROM`/joins: nested loop; for each left row in order, right rows in file order; `ON` evaluated for every pair; `LEFT JOIN` emits one NULL-filled row for an unmatched left row.
141	2. `WHERE` per row. 3. Group keys and aggregate arguments per surviving row. 4. `HAVING` per group. 5. Select expressions per surviving row/group. 6. `ORDER BY` keys. 7. `DISTINCT` (first occurrence kept). 8. Sort. 9. `OFFSET`, then `LIMIT`.
142	
143	`AND` skips its right side when the left is false; `OR` when the left is true. Rows are processed in order within each step; the first failure is reported and no output is produced.
144	
145	### Library API
146	
147	```python
148	minisql.connect(data_dir: str | os.PathLike) -> Connection
149	Connection.execute(sql: str) -> Result
150	Connection.tables() -> list[str]                    # stems, sorted by (lower(), name)
151	Connection.schema(table: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]  # (column, type) in header order
152	@dataclass(frozen=True)
153	class Result: columns: list[str]; types: list[str]; rows: list[tuple]
154	minisql.format_csv(result: Result) -> str
155	minisql.format_table(result: Result) -> str
156	```
157	
158	`types` holds `"INTEGER"`, `"REAL"`, `"TEXT"` or `"NULL"`. Row values are `int`, `float`, `str` or `None`.
159	
160	### Output formats
161	
162	Value text: INTEGER `str(v)`; REAL `repr(v)` (`100.0`, `2.5`, `1e+20`); TEXT verbatim.
163	
164	**CSV** (`--format csv`, default for one-shot): header line, then one line per row, fields joined by `,`, every line terminated by `\n` (also on Windows). NULL is an empty unquoted field. A field is wrapped in `"` (inner `"` doubled) iff it is the empty string, contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, or starts or ends with a space. Header names follow the same quoting.
165	
166	**Table** (`--format table`, default for REPL): cell text is the value text with newline and carriage-return characters replaced by the two-character escapes `\n` and `\r`; NULL is `NULL`. Width of a column = max code-point length of header and cells. Header cells left-aligned; INTEGER/REAL values right-aligned; TEXT and `NULL` left-aligned. Cells joined by ` | `; separator line is `-` × width per column joined by `-+-`; trailing spaces stripped from every line; then `(N rows)` or `(1 row)`. Every line ends with `\n`.
167	
168	### CLI
169	
170	`python -m minisql [--data DIR] [--format csv|table] [SQL]`. With `SQL`: one-shot, print the formatted result to stdout. Without `SQL`: REPL on stdin. stdout and stderr are UTF-8 with `\n`.
171	
172	### REPL
173	
174	- Prompt `minisql> ` when the buffer is empty, `   ...> ` otherwise; written to stdout without newline, flushed, whether or not stdin is a TTY. Input is not echoed.
175	- With an empty buffer, a line whose stripped text starts with `.` is a command; a blank line is ignored. Otherwise the line is appended (joined with `\n`); when the buffer, right-stripped, ends with `;`, it is executed and cleared.
176	- Commands: `.help` (free text), `.tables` (one name per line, `tables()` order), `.schema NAME` (`name TYPE` per line), `.format csv|table`, `.quit` and `.exit`. Unknown command: stderr `unknown command: <text>`.
177	- Results print in the current format (CSV has no row-count footer). Errors print one line to stderr and the session continues; positions are relative to the buffer.
178	- At EOF a non-empty buffer is executed; then exit 0 with nothing further printed. `.quit` exits 0.
179	
180	### Exit codes (one-shot)
181	
182	| Code | Meaning |
183	|---|---|
184	| 0 | success |
185	| 1 | LexError, ParseError, SemanticError, RuntimeError |
186	| 2 | usage error (argparse) |
187	| 3 | IOError |
188	
189	On error stdout is empty and stderr holds exactly the error line plus `\n`. No tracebacks.
190	
191	## Error handling
192	
193	Classes exported from `minisql`, subclassing `MiniSQLError(Exception)`: `LexError`, `ParseError`, `SemanticError`, `QueryRuntimeError`, `DataIOError`, with attributes `kind` (`Lex`/`Parse`/`Semantic`/`Runtime`/`IO`), `line`, `column` (`None` for IO), `message`; `str(err)` is the formatted line.
194	
195	Format: `<Kind>Error at line L, column C: <message>`; IO errors: `IOError: <message>`.
196	
197	| Kind | Message templates | Position |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| Lex | `unexpected character 'X'`, `unterminated string literal`, `unterminated quoted identifier`, `invalid number literal` | offending character / opening quote / literal start |
200	| Parse | `unexpected token 'T'` (T = token source text), `unexpected end of input` | token start / one past last input character |
201	| Semantic | `unknown table 'N'`, `duplicate table name 'N'`, `unknown column 'R'`, `ambiguous column 'R'`, `unknown function 'F'`, `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T1 and T2`, `type mismatch: cannot apply 'OP' to T`, `condition must be numeric, got TEXT`, `aggregate function not allowed here`, `column 'R' must appear in GROUP BY or be used in an aggregate`, `'*' not allowed in aggregate query`, `ORDER BY position N is out of range`, `ORDER BY expression must appear in select list when DISTINCT is used`, `ESCAPE must be a single character` | table/name token; column ref start; operator token (function name for aggregates); condition/expression start; `*`; ordinal; ESCAPE string |
202	| Runtime | `division by zero`, `invalid LIKE pattern` | `/` or `%` token; `LIKE` token |
203	| IO | `data directory not found: DIR` (DIR as given), `ambiguous table file 'N'`, `<file>: empty file`, `<file>: empty column name`, `<file>: duplicate column 'C'`, `<file>: line N: expected K fields, got M`, `<file>: line N: malformed CSV`, `<file>: invalid UTF-8` | none |
204	
205	`N`, `R`, `F` are names as written in the query without quotes (`R` qualified as `q.c`). `OP` is the operator as written for symbols, upper-case for keywords and aggregates (`LIKE`, `IN`, `AND`, `SUM`). `<file>` is the base file name. For `duplicate table name 'N'`, the position is the range-name token of the second `tableref` with that range name (its alias if present, else its table name) and `N` is that range name as written. For `'*' argument only allowed for COUNT`, the position is the `*` token inside the call. For `duplicate column 'C'`, `C` is the second occurrence's header name exactly as written in the CSV. For `malformed CSV`, `N` is the reader's `line_num` at the moment `csv.Error` is raised. Phases run lex → parse → semantic (including IO for referenced tables, in `FROM` order) → execute. The oracle only uses queries containing a single error.
206	
207	## Acceptance criteria
208	
209	Fixture `emp.csv`: `id,name,dept,salary` / `1,Ann,eng,100` / `2,Bob,eng,` / `3,Cid,ops,80` / `4,Dee,,80` / `5,Eve,ops,120`. Fixture `dept.csv`: `code,title` / `eng,Engineering` / `ops,Operations` / `ops,Ops Dup` / `hr,Human Resources`.
210	
211	- **AC1** (R1, R19) `python -m minisql --data D "SELECT 1 AS one"` prints `one\n1\n`, exit 0; no non-stdlib or `sqlite3` import in `minisql/`.
212	- **AC2** (R2, R21) `SELECT * FROM EMP` returns 5 rows; `--data missing` exits 3 with `IOError: data directory not found: missing`.
213	- **AC3** (R3) `schema("emp")` is `[("id","INTEGER"),("name","TEXT"),("dept","TEXT"),("salary","INTEGER")]`.
214	- **AC4** (R4, R21) `SELECT 1 # 2` → `LexError at line 1, column 10: unexpected character '#'`.
215	- **AC5** (R5) `SELECT 1 + 2 * 3, -2 * 3, NOT 1 = 2` → `1 + 2 * 3,-2 * 3,NOT 1 = 2` / `7,-6,1`.
216	- **AC6** (R6) `select NAME from Emp e where E.Id = 1` → `name` / `Ann` (header from the CSV, not the query).
217	- **AC7** (R7) `SELECT name + 1 FROM emp` → `SemanticError at line 1, column 13: type mismatch: cannot apply '+' to TEXT and INTEGER`.
218	- **AC8** (R8) `SELECT 7 / 2, -7 / 2, 7 % -2, 7.0 / 2, NULL / 0` → `3,-3,1,3.5,`.
219	- **AC9** (R9) `SELECT name FROM emp WHERE dept NOT IN ('eng', NULL)` → header only.
220	- **AC10** (R10) `SELECT salary * 2, name AS n FROM emp WHERE id = 1` → header `salary * 2,n`, row `200,Ann`.
221	- **AC11** (R17) `connect(D).execute("SELECT AVG(salary) FROM emp")` has `types == ["REAL"]`, `rows == [(95.0,)]`.
222	- **AC12** (R2-R21) Behaviour specified in the Language reference, Interface contract and Error handling sections is reproduced exactly (byte-for-byte output, exit codes and error lines) by hidden tests.
223

2	
3	## Authority and outcome
4	
5	Implement the entire root `contract.md` R1–R21 / AC1–AC12, with the architecture and pytest requirement in `brief.md`. The feature specification organizes but cannot override that authority. No required scope is deferred. Decisions D1–D7 in feature-specification.md §8 resolve unspecified edges; an explicit contract rule always wins.
6	
7	## Architecture and ownership
8	
9	| Surface | Owner | Purpose |
10	|---|---|---|
11	| minisql/errors.py, model.py, lexer.py, ast.py, parser.py, initial __init__.py | T1 | Error classes, frozen Result, positioned tokens, source-preserving AST/parser |
12	| minisql/catalog.py | T2 | Directory discovery, strict CSV loading and inference |
13	| minisql/formatting.py | T3 | Pure exact CSV and aligned-table strings |
14	| minisql/semantic.py, executor.py, connection.py; final __init__.py | T4 | Typed/bound analysis, ordered execution, public API integration |
15	| minisql/__main__.py, cli.py, root README.md | T5 | One-shot/REPL and usage documentation |
16	| tests/test_contract.py, test_regressions.py, test_imports.py | T6 | Independent contract-wide acceptance/regression coverage |
17	
18	Each task owns its corresponding test files as listed in the task. Workers may not edit another task's surface without orchestrator coordination and recording the consequence in both task notes and handoff. Orchestrator does not edit product code/tests; fixes return to geeky-coder.
19	
20	## Cross-module integration contract
21	
22	### Foundation protocol
23	
24	T1 exposes `MiniSQLError(message, line=None, column=None)` and subclasses with class-specific kinds; subclasses accept message then line/column. `DataIOError(message)` has None positions. Attributes and str formatting exactly contract. `model.Result` is frozen dataclass with list columns, list types, list tuple rows. Initial __init__ exports Result and errors only, avoiding imports of modules not yet present.
25	
26	T1 chooses and documents concrete lexer/AST/parser interfaces in T1 notes. They must expose token kind/raw text/decoded value/start/end/line/column, parser entry `parse(sql) -> Query` (lexer may be invoked inside), complete AST for contract grammar, distinct parenthesis metadata, source spans and operator/name/star/ESCAPE tokens. Preserve raw source for output heading and resolved-independent structure. T4 consumes those interfaces; T1 notes are a required handoff, not a change to the frozen task body.
27	
28	### Data protocol
29	
30	T2 exposes `Catalog(data_dir)` (immediate validation), `tables() -> list[str]`, `load(name, line=1, column=1) -> Table`, `schema(name)` where Table has name, columns list[str], types list[str], rows list[tuple]. Unknown table raises SemanticError at provided coordinates; ambiguous/corrupt data DataIOError. A load call rereads disk; executor may reuse a table within one execute but never across execute calls. Semantic analysis loads table refs in FROM order and resolves range names itself.
31	
32	T2 imports errors from errors.py; no dependency on parser/semantic. During the independent phase tests may use the agreed protocol when T1 is simultaneously creating errors; collect integration validation after all workers return.
33	
34	### Formatting protocol
35	
36	T3 implements `format_csv(result: Result) -> str` and `format_table(result: Result) -> str` in formatting.py, imports Result from model only, never touches streams. T3 tests may construct Result. It must exactly preserve NULL/empty TEXT distinction.
37	
38	### Engine protocol
39	
40	T4 exposes `Connection(data_dir)`, connect, execute, tables/schema and full __init__ API. Execute obtains AST, binds all references/types before executor calls. Semantic and executor must remain distinct recognizable layers; implementation may use bound node records or annotations but must preserve raw AST source metadata. Formats reexported from formatting. No import-time stream mutation.
41	
42	## Implementation phases and dependency graph
43	
44	### Phase 1 — Foundations (T1, T2, T3)
45	
46	Dispatch up to three independent non-overlapping workers concurrently. T2 and T3 share only agreed protocols; T1 creates errors/model promptly. No worker edits shared __init__ except T1. Completion commands cover all three surfaces after return. All stay In Review until a single reviewer subagent gives individual task verdicts and phase `READY TO ADVANCE`. Then Done + check-dod/kanban gates and phase commit.
47	
48	### Phase 2 — Typed engine (T4)
49	
50	Depends on Done T1/T2/T3 and phase-1 READY. Implement binder and explicit executor pipeline together because resolved identities, aggregate slots and execution contexts are tightly coupled. Largest task; split internally into analysis then execution, but its scope is fully specified. Use exact contract, not a generic SQL engine. Independent reviewer checks all T4 ACs and collective engine requirements, returns task verdict plus READY TO ADVANCE. Fixes by coder only. Then Done/gates and phase commit.
51	
52	### Phase 3 — Delivery and acceptance (T5, T6)
53	
54	Both depend on Done T4; run concurrently with distinct test/product surfaces. T6 tests engine and format/public API, not T5 CLI until integration; T5 owns subprocess CLI/REPL tests. Collect all, run combined full suite/import/compile checks. Independent reviewer returns both task verdicts and phase READY TO ADVANCE, including contract-wide gaps. Done/gates and phase commit. Final stage remains the separately required three-lane impl-review.
55	
56	Dependency edges: T1/T2/T3 → T4 → T5/T6. No cycles. T2/T3 use fixed foundational protocols without completion dependency, enabled by common integration validation and no overlapping writes. Worker scheduling must honor explicit task dependencies; Backlog tasks promoted only after dependencies Done.
57	
58	## Engine design details
59	
60	### Lex / parse
61	
62	Handwritten complete lexer, recursive-descent parser. Positions code points, LF-only lines. Exact ASCII regexes, malformed continuation checks; signs separate. Precedence and non-associative comparison exact. Quoted names/strings decode doubles while retaining original spans. Full tokenize before parse. Parenthesis node/flag preserved for headings/bare ORDER but ignored for structural keys. No FROM yields one empty row.
63	
64	### Semantic
65	
66	Load referenced CSVs in FROM order after parse; no unrelated reads. Scoped ON binding per introduced prefix; aliases hide original qualifiers, duplicate ranges positioned at second range token. Expand wildcards; preserve output headers. Bind resolved column indexes and static types for every expression irrespective of rows, filters, short circuit or pagination. Type operators and conditions exactly, no bool outputs.
67	
68	Discover aggregates in select/HAVING/order; reject forbidden placement/nesting/star. Recursively validate grouping by bound structural keys. Group keys compare column identity, operators, typed literal values, operand order; no text matching/algebraic rewriting. Resolve bare ORDER alias/ordinal before input expression binding; alias wins, duplicate aliases ambiguous. DISTINCT restricts order to selected structure or alias/ordinal. Record projected output indexes for alias/ordinal reuse.
69	
70	### Execute
71	
72	Materialized stage barriers: joins → WHERE → grouping keys/all aggregate arguments → HAVING → select → ORDER keys → first DISTINCT → stable sort → OFFSET/LIMIT. Nested-loop join order and first-seen group order. Global aggregate group exists even empty. Distinct and grouping equate None; normal predicates do not. All aggregate arguments evaluated in input order before HAVING. All projection before order-key evaluation. LIMIT 0 cannot suppress faults.
73	
74	Use explicit 3VL; only AND/OR guaranteed short circuit. NULL arithmetic before zero checks; integer quotient exact truncation (abs quotient/sign), remainder dividend-signed; real math.fmod. LIKE whole-string newline-capable matcher with strict ESCAPE policy. Stable multi-key comparator handles NULL and DESC without reversing tie order. Return complete Result before any CLI writes.
75	
76	### Output / CLI
77	
78	Custom CSV quoting iff prescribed conditions, not csv.writer defaults. Table escapes before measuring, numeric actual values right, NULL left. CLI reconfigure UTF-8/LF only inside main; argparse usage exit 2. Validate data before SQL lexing. One-shot error stdout empty; engine error one stderr line, codes 1/3. REPL prompt/buffer state follows literal textual suffix and EOF rules, .tables/.schema/.format/help/quit/exit, errors continue.
79	
80	## Validation strategy
81	
82	Each task supplies exact pytest commands plus compile checks. `python3` denotes available host interpreter, not a claim that its version satisfies stack target. Record runtime with each suite. Current host default 3.9.6; installed 3.14 variants killed before version output. Product targets >=3.11; maintain compatible stdlib syntax where feasible to enable local checks; do not impose a needless runtime rejection. Seek existing supported interpreter without installation; if unavailable, report as unexecuted-runtime warning and review source compatibility. Windows/Linux byte behavior designed/tested structurally but no unrun OS claimed.
83	
84	Required task suites: lexer/parser, catalog, formatting, semantic, executor, API, CLI, REPL, contract anchors/regressions/import audit. Final `python3 -m pytest -q`, `python3 -m compileall -q minisql`, and stdlib/no sqlite/SQL-engine audit. Exact numeric outcomes and tested revision/content recorded in notes. Tests for all contract sections, not just examples. No external SQL differential oracle.
85	
86	## Review / Done / commit gates
87	
88	Before implementation: validate planning folder, task schema and kanban plus independent plan-review. During work: validate kanban after each lane move. At phase end single independent code-reviewer receives task contracts, worker evidence, concrete changed files and validation commands; returns per-task verdicts and phase READY TO ADVANCE (last phase included). Required fixes coder-owned and reviewed again. Bare claims insufficient; reuse valid revision evidence and rerun invalidated/missing checks.

Commit per phase, message lists task IDs and passes check-commit; attribution per session. Never push/force/amend/no-verify. Preserve frozen artifacts throughout implementation. If Blocked, checkpoint notes/kanban/handoff then stop. Final impl-review separately mandatory, fixes preapproved, repeat until overall PASS or budget/capability blocker.
